john.11.p1.b1.text: At this time a man named Lazarus was sick. He lived in Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.

john.11.p1.b2.text: So the sisters sent word to Jesus,

john.11.p1.b3.text: Lord, the one You love is sick.

john.11.p2.b1.text: This sickness will not end in death. No, it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.

john.11.p2.b2.text: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.

john.11.p2.b3.text: So on hearing that Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was for two days,

john.11.p3.b1.text: Let us go back to Judea.

john.11.p3.b2.text: Rabbi, … the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?

john.11.p3.b3.text: Are there not twelve hours of daylight? If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.

john.11.p3.b4.text: But if anyone walks at night, he will stumble, because he has no light.”

john.11.p4.b1.text: Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.

john.11.p4.b2.text: Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better.

john.11.p4.b4.text: Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.

john.11.p5.b1.text: When Jesus arrived, He found that Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb.

john.11.p5.b2.text: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them in the loss of their brother.

john.11.p5.b3.text: So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet Him; but Mary stayed at home.

john.11.p6.b1.text: Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.

john.11.p6.b3.text: I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.

john.11.p7.b1.text: I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.

john.11.p7.b2.text: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die. Do you believe this?”

john.11.p7.b3.text: Yes, Lord, … I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world.

john.11.p8.b1.text: The Teacher is here and is asking for you.

john.11.p8.b2.text: And when Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to Him.

john.11.p8.b3.text: When the Jews … saw how quickly she got up and went out, they followed her, supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there.

john.11.p9.b1.text: Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.

john.11.p9.b2.text: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled.

john.11.p10.b3.text: Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?

john.11.p11.b1.text: Jesus, once again deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance.

john.11.p11.b4.text: Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?

john.11.p12.b1.text: So they took away the stone.

john.11.p12.b2.text: Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.

john.11.p12.b3.text: I knew that You always hear Me, but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here, so they may believe that You sent Me.”

john.11.p13.b1.text: After Jesus had said this, He called out in a loud voice,

john.11.p14.b1.text: The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth.

john.11.p14.b2.text: Unwrap him and let him go,

john.11.p15.b1.text: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him.

john.11.p15.b2.text: But some of them went to the Pharisees

john.11.p15.b3.text: and told them what Jesus had done.

john.11.p16.b1.text: Then the chief priests and Pharisees convened the Sanhedrin and said,

john.11.p16.b2.text: What are we to do? This man is performing many signs.

john.11.p16.b3.text: If we let Him go on like this, everyone will believe in Him,

john.11.p16.b4.text: and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.

john.11.p17.b1.text: But one of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them,

john.11.p17.b3.text: You do not realize that it is better for you that one man die for the people than that the whole nation perish.”

john.11.p18.b1.text: Caiaphas did not say this on his own. Instead, as high priest that year, he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation,

john.11.p18.b2.text: and not only for the nation, but also for the scattered children of God, to gather them together into one.

john.11.p18.b3.text: So from that day on they plotted to kill Him.

john.11.p19.b1.text: As a result, Jesus no longer went about publicly among the Jews, but He withdrew to a town … in an area near the wilderness.

john.11.p19.b3.text: And He stayed there with the disciples.

john.11.p20.b1.text: Now the Jewish Passover was near,

john.11.p20.b2.text: and many people went up from the country to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the Passover.

john.11.p20.b3.text: What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?

john.11.p21.b1.text: But the chief priests and Pharisees had given orders

john.11.p21.b2.text: that anyone who knew where He was must report it,

john.11.p21.b3.text: so that they could arrest Him.
